target_customer: Homeowners in Spain and Southern Europe who want solar, storage and heat pumps without upfront payment
problem: Most households cannot or will not pay thousands upfront for solar panels, so rooftop adoption in sunny Spain lagged.
business_model: Subscription: customer pays a monthly fee (reported as about 40 EUR per month over 20 years) funded by project debt, company owns the installation
product_category: Residential solar as a service and home electrification

founders.name: Wouter Draijer
education: Teaches in the ESADE MBA program (later)
founders.background_notes: Dutch, YES!Delft alumnus and angel investor; was prompted to start after noticing how few Barcelona rooftops had solar. A source says he stepped down as CEO in August 2025 (aggregator, unverified). Euronews gave his age as 29 in April 2024, which is not an age at founding.

founders.name: Victor Gardrinier
founders.background_notes: His YC profile claims the company grew from zero to 10M USD ARR.

technical_complexity.rationale: Installation logistics and project finance were the hard parts, not the technology; the software layer was modest.

defensibility.rationale: Access to debt and a trusted brand help, but installers and rivals such as Otovo and Sunhero offered similar zero upfront deals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; SolarMente acquired installer Eltex in October 2024 per trade coverage, then reportedly entered insolvency in 2026.

market_need_then: Spain had high sun and rising power prices in 2021, but few rooftops with solar; the CEO argued most Spaniards would not pay upfront.

branding.domain_note: solarmente.es, a Spanish country domain; site returned HTTP 503 when fetched.
branding.brand_signature: Leonardo DiCaprio as a named investor, publicized in March 2024 as a trust builder
branding.community_and_virality: Wide press pickup of the DiCaprio news (TechCrunch, Tech.eu, Euronews, Euro Weekly News).

brand_strength.rationale: Celebrity investor drove broad European press in 2024 and founders said recognizable names helped rebuild trust; no evidence of organic community.

outcome_analysis: SolarMente joined YC in Summer 2021, scaled to a reported 65 staff and about 10M USD ARR, financed with 50M in debt in 2023 and a DiCaprio backed seed in 2024. The YC directory lists it as Inactive, and one Spanish source dated May 2026 reports an insolvency filing in February 2026. No source gives the cause, so it is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: Seed amount conflicts: 2M USD (Carta founder interview), 1.8M EUR (another outlet); YC page says about 5M from YC, Climate Capital, Soma Capital, Plug and Play, DiCaprio and others, not itemized. Insolvency rests on one article (asest.es, May 2026) listing debt near 197K EUR, unverified. Founding year ranges from 2019 to 2021 across sources; 2020 follows a directory saying the first subscription offer was by summer 2020, uncertain. Competitor search found Otovo and Sunhero with 2023 sources only, so none are listed as of 2021.
